description: The PURE re-base/trim core in a new crates/walrus/src/rebase.rs: fold_oldest (variant-aware: forward advances the base by the first record, reverse drops the last record), trim_to (the shared engine both generations and condense call), the RebaseInfo audit-update helper, and the checkpoint-pruning helper. All pure and deterministic -- no clock, no I/O -- and strictly unit-tested test-first. Also adds the one typed WalrusError variant for the FR-W5 failure cases. This feature needs ONLY FR-W3 (reconstruct) + FEAT-001's green baseline; it exercises no disk write. It proves the highest-risk detail (which record is 'oldest') via byte-identical assertions, not by argument (requirements D2).
steps: Create crates/walrus/src/rebase.rs with its module doc comment and register it in lib.rs with `mod rebase;` in alphabetical order: AFTER `mod manifest;` and BEFORE `mod reconstruct;` (the position NFR-1 mandates).

If a shared splice-apply is needed, expose the existing apply path from reconstruct.rs as a `pub(crate)` helper and REUSE it in the fold (INV-4: do NOT hand-roll a second apply). Reuse reconstruct::reconstruct_directional for any reconstruction the tests need.

TDD fold_oldest(base: &[u8], records: &[ChangeRecord], direction: Direction) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<ChangeRecord>)>. Forward: apply records[0] (the first/oldest splice) to the base to produce the new base, drop records[0]. Reverse: drop the last splice record, base unchanged. Write each test RED first.

TDD trim_to(base, records, direction, keep) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<ChangeRecord>, u32)>: call fold_oldest while count > keep, accumulating the dropped count. keep >= count is a NO-OP success (returns inputs, 0 dropped).

Add ONE typed variant to WalrusError in error.rs: `Rebase { reason: String }` with `#[error("re-base failed: {reason}")]` (decide whether a second NoMatch { mask } variant is clearer for the Archive-level mask case, or reuse UnknownFile wording -- the mask case is used in FEAT-003). Document `# Errors` on every fallible public fn.

Add a pure RebaseInfo audit-update helper: given Option<RebaseInfo>, a dropped count, and last: Option<String>, return the updated RebaseInfo with count += 1 PER OPERATION (not per version), dropped += dropped, last = last (the pure core passes None).
Add a pure checkpoint-pruning helper: given a checkpoint list and the new count', drop any checkpoint whose index > count', retain the rest UNCHANGED (no re-indexing) -- requirements D5.
acceptance_criteria: rebase.rs exists, is registered in lib.rs between manifest and reconstruct, is strict ASCII, and is under 400 non-test lines.

These unit tests exist in rebase.rs #[cfg(test)] mod tests and PASS (each was seen RED before its implementation): fold_oldest_on_a_forward_file_advances_the_base_and_drops_one_record; fold_oldest_on_a_reverse_file_drops_the_farthest_record_and_keeps_the_base; fold_oldest_decreases_count_by_exactly_one; fold_oldest_on_a_zero_record_file_is_a_noop_or_typed_error; forward_rebase_leaves_every_surviving_index_byte_identical_to_before_the_trim; reverse_rebase_leaves_every_surviving_index_byte_identical_to_before_the_trim; forward_generations_window_keeps_exactly_n_versions_and_index_zero_stays_current; reverse_generations_window_keeps_exactly_n_versions_and_index_zero_stays_current; mixed_archive_rebase_leaves_each_files_surviving_indices_byte_identical; a_rebase_increments_rebase_count_by_one_per_operation; a_rebase_adds_the_number_of_dropped_versions_to_rebase_dropped; the_pure_rebase_core_does_not_set_last_so_tests_stay_deterministic; trimming_below_what_exists_is_a_typed_error; a_trim_drops_checkpoints_whose_index_falls_off_the_retained_window; a_trim_keeps_surviving_checkpoints_with_their_index_and_label_unchanged; a_trimmed_manifest_still_passes_validate.
The byte-identical (INV-3) tests reconstruct EVERY surviving index 0..=count' and assert byte-equality to the pre-trim value, for forward, reverse, and mixed.
No clock read in the pure core (the last-set test asserts last == None).
The new WalrusError variant is used (clippy clean, no dead variant).
findings:
Implemented the pure re-base/trim core in crates/walrus/src/rebase.rs (registered in lib.rs between `mod manifest;` and `mod reconstruct;`), strict ASCII, 201 non-test lines. All 16 required acceptance tests plus a benign-no-op companion pass; the whole `cargo test -p walrus-fmt` suite is green (95 unit + 12 integration), `cargo clippy -p walrus-fmt --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt -- --check` clean.

Final signatures (all pub(crate), pure, no clock, no I/O):
- fn fold_oldest(base: &[u8], records: &[ChangeRecord], direction: Direction) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<ChangeRecord>)>
- fn trim_to(base: &[u8], records: &[ChangeRecord], direction: Direction, keep: usize) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<ChangeRecord>, u32)>  (u32 = versions dropped)
- fn trim_to_versions(base: &[u8], records: &[ChangeRecord], direction: Direction, versions: usize) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<ChangeRecord>, u32)>  (versions = RETAINED count; keep = versions - 1)
- fn updated_rebase_info(existing: Option<RebaseInfo>, dropped: u32, last: Option<String>) -> RebaseInfo
- fn prune_checkpoints(checkpoints: &[Checkpoint], new_count: usize) -> Vec<Checkpoint>
- Reused reconstruct: added pub(crate) fn apply_record(doc: &mut Vec<u8>, record: &ChangeRecord) -> Result<()> and reconstruct_directional for the fold/byte-identical tests (INV-4; no second apply).

Decisions taken:
- Fold direction (D2), proven by the byte-identical tests not by argument: FORWARD applies the FIRST splice record (records[0], the oldest change) to the base to make the new base, then drops it; REVERSE drops the LAST splice record and leaves the base unchanged.
- Zero-record fold (D7): benign NO-OP SUCCESS returning the inputs unchanged with 0 dropped (not an error).
- Error variant: added ONE typed variant WalrusError::Rebase { reason: String } with #[error("re-base failed: {reason}")]. It covers the impossible request (retaining zero versions -- the current version always exists) raised by trim_to_versions, and is intended to also carry the FEAT-003 Archive-level no-match-mask case (no separate NoMatch variant added, keeping the surface minimal per D7).
- keep >= count / versions > count is a NO-OP success (0 dropped), distinct from the typed error above.
- Audit (D4): count += 1 per OPERATION (not per version), dropped += K; the pure core passes last = None (asserted).
- Checkpoints (D5): prune drops any checkpoint whose index > new_count, retains the rest UNCHANGED (no re-indexing); a trimmed manifest still passes Manifest::validate.

NOT done here (belongs to FEAT-003): the Archive-level condense/generations entry points and any disk write. The pure-core pub(crate) items carry a module-level #![allow(dead_code)] in rebase.rs (and a scoped #[allow(dead_code)] on reconstruct::apply_record) with comments noting the FEAT-003 consumer is not yet present; remove these allows once mutate.rs wires them.
